name: wayland

engine.notes: "direct-compile": not any of crt-port-build.py's own configure/amalgamation/android_host_tool systems, and (2026-08-24 rewrite) not Meson/Ninja either -- tools/build_wayland.py drives every compile/link step itself via tools/crt-cc directly, replicating upstream's own generated-file mechanics (embed.py's DTD-to-header format, wayland-version.h.in's substitution, wayland-scanner's own client-header/public-code CLI modes) rather than delegating to any build-orchestration tool at all. Kept alongside libcrtgfx/third_party/skia/recipe.json's own GN/Ninja external build (outside porting/recipes/, which only the generic configure/amalgamation engine globs) for the same class of reason -- an external, non-CMake build -- even though this one now needs no external tool beyond the C compiler itself. libcrtgfx/CMakeLists.txt reads this file's own source.* fields at configure time via CMake's string(JSON ...) and feeds them to tools/fetch_wayland.py as plain CLI flags, exactly matching the Skia recipe's own wiring.

notes: Scope, decided 2026-08-24, narrowed twice that same day: first from full core (scanner+client+server+cursor+egl) down to scanner+client only (wayland-server/-cursor/-egl deferred -- crtgfx-wayland-smoke, the only current consumer, only needs wayland-client), then the *build mechanism* itself was replaced -- see the next note. wayland-protocols (xdg-shell.xml and friends) stays deferred regardless: core wayland.xml alone is what wayland-client.c itself needs, no external protocol package required to prove the external-build pipeline works for real.

Build mechanism replaced 2026-08-24, at the user's own explicit direction after being shown a manual embedded-cross-compile guide: the original design (Meson/Ninja, still using tools/crt-cc as the actual compiler) worked in principle but needed meson/ninja/pkg-config as real host build tools -- this project's own sandboxed tooling cannot install host packages (the same class of gap already hit for `lld` earlier this session), and real embedded target environments often cannot host a Python+Meson toolchain either. tools/build_wayland.py now drives every compile/link step directly instead, matching this project's own 'own the toolchain' philosophy more literally: the only non-project-owned things this build depends on now are the C compiler itself (already true everywhere else) and this project's own already-ported expat/libffi. No wayland-client.pc is generated any more either (there is no Meson pkgconfig module to generate one) -- crtgfx-wayland-smoke links the static archive and libffi.a by explicit full path instead, matching porting/recipes/*.json's own roundtrip-static test convention.

Static archive only (libwayland-client.a), no shared .so yet: deliberately avoids the two-copies-of-this-project's-own-libc risk a shared libwayland-client.so (itself linked against this project's shared libc.so, matching how tools/crt-cc's own shared_mode already links every other -shared output here) would create for a smoke-test executable that otherwise links statically -- and a real .so needs its own SONAME-versioning ceremony (matching tools/crt-port-build.py::build_amalgamation_shared_library()'s own convention) that has no current consumer to justify yet.

Real, general CRT/PAL gaps were found and filled compiling Wayland's own real sources against this project's libc, not routed around -- three found verifying Linux first, two more found extending to Windows the same day (all five are cross-platform fixes, not Linux-only, once the Windows pass was done): (1) SO_PEERCRED/struct ucred (include/sys/socket.h) -- src/wayland-os.c's own wl_os_socket_peercred() has a hard `#elif defined(SO_PEERCRED)` / `#else #error "Don't know how to read ucred on this platform"` with no portable fallback (unlike HAVE_ACCEPT4/HAVE_SYS_UCRED_H/HAVE_BROKEN_MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC/HAVE_GETTID, each of which DOES have one -- see tools/build_wayland.py's own generate_config_header() docstring); added the real Linux UAPI value (17) and struct layout -- declared cross-platform (a Windows compile needs src/wayland-os.c too), documented as compile-only on Windows (no real Winsock AF_UNIX peer-credential query backs it, and nothing calls this function at runtime there anyway, unreachable without a real compositor). MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC/MSG_DONTWAIT/MSG_NOSIGNAL (also include/sys/socket.h, real Linux values, same cross-platform-but-compile-only-on-Windows treatment) needed by src/connection.c's own read/write path. (2) ppoll() (include/poll.h, libc/src/poll.c) -- src/wayland-client.c's own dispatch loop calls it with no __linux__ guard of its own, so it needs to work on every target too; rewritten fully portable (no OS guard at all) in terms of the already cross-platform poll(), mirroring how sys/select.h's own pselect() is already a portable wrapper around select() -- the raw Linux-only __crt_sys_ppoll syscall trampoline is no longer used by this function at all (poll() itself still uses it internally on Linux). (3) epoll_create() (include/sys/epoll.h, libc/src/epoll.c) -- wl_os_epoll_create_cloexec()'s own epoll_create1-unavailable fallback path (dead code on any real kernel, still unconditionally compiled); implemented in terms of the already cross-platform epoll_create1(0) (itself already ENOSYS-returning on non-Linux), so no separate Windows handling was needed here. (4) SOCK_CLOEXEC (include/sys/socket.h, now #include <fcntl.h>) -- src/wayland-os.c's own wl_os_socket_cloexec() -- a real Linux kernel ABI fact (the kernel reuses O_CLOEXEC's own bit value here), added as `#define SOCK_CLOEXEC O_CLOEXEC` matching sys/epoll.h's own already-established EPOLL_CLOEXEC precedent exactly. (5) tools/crt-port-build.py's own AR/RANLIB/STRIP defaults (a general, Wayland-adjacent fix, not a Wayland-specific gap -- see HISTORY.md's own entry for the full separate trail).

Windows also needed three build-orchestration fixes in the new scripts themselves (tools/build_wayland.py/tools/test_crtgfx_wayland_smoke.py), none of them CRT/PAL gaps: missing POSIX-form PATH so tools/crt-cc's own internal printf/sed calls resolve (an earlier version of this project's own comments incorrectly claimed this script was exempt from the POSIX-PATH requirement tools/build_skia.py's own GN build needs -- it is not, corrected in place); a new --windows-sdk-libpath flag (wired from libcrtgfx/CMakeLists.txt's own ${CRT_WINDOWS_KERNEL32_LIB}) since this is the first script in the project to link a real Windows executable directly via crt-cc rather than through regular CMake's own target_link_libraries(${CRT_WINDOWS_SYSTEM_LIBS}); and a CRT_HOST_CC omission specific to tools/test_crtgfx_wayland_smoke.py's own separate env setup (tools/build_wayland.py already had this fix, the smoke script's own copy of the same PATH-narrowing logic had not been updated to match).

Verified for real, not just 'it built' (2026-08-24), on both hosts: Linux x64/WSL -- crtgfx-wayland-smoke fetched Wayland, built wayland-scanner, generated the client protocol bindings, built and installed libwayland-client.a, then compiled and ran wayland_client_smoke -- which found a real, live Wayland compositor already reachable in the verifying session's own WSL environment (WSLg's own Weston/RDP-based one) and completed a genuine wl_registry wire-protocol round trip against it (20 real globals enumerated, including weston_rdprail_shell/weston_screenshooter/wl_compositor/wl_shm/xdg_wm_base/wl_seat), not merely the designed 'no compositor, build/link verified' headless fallback. Full ctest: 104/104. Windows x64 (this session's own dev machine) -- the identical pipeline built wayland-scanner.exe, libwayland-client.a, and wayland_client_smoke.exe; the smoke binary correctly reported `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is invalid or not set` from inside the library itself and hit the designed graceful headless fallback (no real compositor on this machine), printing `wayland_client_smoke: ok`. Full ctest: 121/121 after a full default rebuild (not a stale re-run). See HISTORY.md's 2026-08-24 entries for the complete trail, including the general CMakeLists.txt fix (CRT_BUILD_PRESET_NAME) the Linux verification run itself surfaced, and a recurring (twice, unrelated to Wayland) transient bootstrap-libc++ ordering artifact hit re-verifying Windows.

Pinned, not floating (matching libcrtgfx/third_party/skia/recipe.json's own policy and its own stated reasoning): source.ref/source.expected_commit are the real commit gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland.git's own `1.26.0` tag dereferences to, captured via `git ls-remote https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland.git refs/tags/1.26.0 refs/tags/1.26.0^{}` on 2026-08-24 (the `^{}` form is the annotated tag's own dereferenced commit SHA, not the tag object's own SHA -- `87cc8a8728a923fc57938faa81ba0e74f34ecdc7`, not `5f430e41167dd359b70fb5e9f584ba2dc058e4cc`). 1.26.0 (2026-07-16) was the latest stable release at pin time. Re-pin by re-running the same git ls-remote command and updating both source.ref and source.expected_commit (and this note's own date), never by reverting either to empty/floating.

source.sparse_paths is empty (a full, non-sparse checkout): confirmed for real (2026-08-24) that the whole upstream repo is small (a handful of MB, no vendored third-party content or generated-doc assets the way Skia's own repo has) -- no need for Skia's own cone-mode trimming machinery here. --depth 1 alone (see tools/fetch_wayland.py) already keeps this fetch small.

source.sync_deps is false and stays false: Wayland has no DEPS-style third-party dependency-sync step at all (unlike Skia's git-sync-deps) -- this field only exists so this recipe's own schema shape matches libcrtgfx/third_party/skia/recipe.json's exactly, for whoever reads both side by side.

expat (porting/recipes/expat.json, shared-pass on Linux/Windows as of 2026-08-24) is needed to build wayland-scanner itself (src/scanner.c's own unconditional `#include <expat.h>`). libffi (porting/recipes/libffi.json, partial on Linux/Windows, configure-pass on macOS -- an existing port, not new) is needed for the wayland-client build (connection.c's own closure-based argument marshaling). Both recipes already install into the *same* shared port_prefix per preset build directory (crt-port-build.py's own convention -- every porting/recipes/*.json port lands in one out/<preset>/port-tests/install), so tools/build_wayland.py's own single --port-prefix flag (not two separate ones) points at that one shared prefix's include/lib, where both are found by explicit path (no pkg-config/.pc resolution any more, see the build-mechanism note above).

When this recipe is next touched: verify this note's own workload/scope claims still hold before extending it (e.g. adding wayland-server/wayland-protocols later should get its own dated note here, matching this file's own established discipline, not a silent edit to the notes above).
